discover_titles: Why Are NFL London Games Struggling to Sell Out?
Ticket Prices and 'Team Fatigue' Hit NFL London Demand
NFL's Global Expansion Impacts UK Fan Engagement
spot: NFL games in London are seeing an unusual number of unsold seats for upcoming October 2026 matchups, a departure from their historical quick sell-outs. Fans like Matt Cullen cite rising ticket prices and "team fatigue" as key reasons for the decline in demand, despite London being a crucial international market for the league.
content_html:
Key Developments

For the first time in years, several NFL games scheduled for London in October 2026 are struggling to sell out. While the Week 5 game between the Philadelphia Eagles and Jacksonville Jaguars at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium saw tickets snapped up quickly, the Jacksonville Jaguars vs. Houston Texans matchup at Wembley Stadium still had swaths of unsold seats over the weekend. Similarly, tickets for the Indianapolis Colts vs. Washington Commanders game on October 4 at Tottenham remained available two months after going on sale to the public.

Long-time attendee Matt Cullen, who has been to every London regular-season game since 2007, expressed concern, stating, "It will just be really, really interesting what the future of the London games looks like because they’re not selling to the potential anymore that they used to." Cullen attributed the shift to "a little bit around team fatigue... a lot of it’s around cost." Price hikes implemented from 2025 are still a point of contention among fans.

Dori Dunai, a London-based Green Bay Packers fan on the NFL UK mailing list, confirmed the unusual availability, noting she has been receiving weekly emails about Colts-Commanders tickets. "All other years tickets were gone on the day of sale and heard nothing more of tickets," Dunai said.

The operational management of the games differs; the Jaguars-Texans game is Jacksonville-run, meaning the team manages its own ticketing and operations, a practice since 2022. The NFL itself runs the two Tottenham games. This season, the NFL is playing a record nine international games, including new venues like Melbourne, Australia, which hosts its first game between the Los Angeles Rams and San Francisco 49ers. Other European cities such as Germany, Spain, and France are also hosting games, providing fans with more choices and potentially impacting London's demand.

Key Takeaways

  • Several NFL London games in October 2026 are experiencing unprecedented unsold seats, a significant departure from historical quick sell-outs.
  • Fan sentiment indicates that rising ticket prices and a phenomenon described as "team fatigue" are the primary factors contributing to the decline in demand.
  • The NFL's expanded international schedule, which includes new European host cities, may be diversifying fan attention and impacting London's long-standing appeal.

Why It Matters

London has historically been a cornerstone of the NFL's international expansion efforts, hosting regular-season games since 2007 and serving as a crucial market for global fan engagement. The current struggle to sell out games, particularly for matchups that would have historically been in high demand, signals a potential shift in the landscape of the NFL's UK presence. This trend raises questions about the sustainability of the current pricing model and the impact of the league's broader international strategy on established markets. For the NFL, maintaining fan enthusiasm and affordability in key international hubs like London will be critical as it continues its global expansion.
